stem: The nursing process is best described as which of the following?
options: The totality of actions and inactions toward achieving the purpose of quality nursing care
A single, isolated task performed only once per patient admission
A purely administrative billing procedure with no clinical relevance
A legal document used only in cases of malpractice litigation

stem: Which of the following is explicitly listed as a purpose of the nursing process?
options: Maintaining the client's health
Maximizing hospital bed turnover regardless of client outcome
Eliminating the need for any physician involvement in care
Reducing the number of nurses required per shift

stem: Besides maintaining health, the nursing process also aims to provide care that returns the client to a state of health OR helps them achieve which outcome?
options: A peaceful death
An extended, medically futile resuscitation regardless of client wishes
Permanent dependence on hospital services
Complete isolation from family members

stem: Maximizing quality of life within the nursing process purposes involves improving the client's resources and doing what else?
options: Making appropriate referrals for community health
Withholding all referrals until the client specifically requests them in writing
Limiting all care strictly to the hospital setting with no community involvement
Avoiding any discussion of resources with the client or family

stem: Which nursing theorist's framework is specifically listed among the theoretical foundations of the nursing process, based on a hierarchy of needs?
options: Maslow
Florence Nightingale
Virginia Henderson
Dorothy Orem

stem: Which theoretical foundation of the nursing process is specifically based on 14 fundamental needs?
options: Virginia Henderson's component model
Florence Nightingale's environmental model
Sister Callista Roy's Adaptation model
Gordon Marjory's Patterns of Human Responses

stem: Which theoretical foundation of the nursing process is specifically known as the Adaptation model?
options: Sister Callista Roy's model
Dorothy Orem's theory
Gordon Marjory's framework
Florence Nightingale's model

stem: According to one definition given, the nursing process is a structured approach to nursing practice and its evaluation, based on which overall method?
options: A problem-solving approach
A purely intuitive, unstructured approach with no method at all
An approach based exclusively on physician orders with no independent nursing judgment
An approach limited strictly to documentation with no direct patient contact

stem: According to the definitions given, nursing process focuses on treating the unique responses of individuals or groups to which type of occurrence?
options: Potential alteration in health
Routine administrative scheduling only
Unrelated financial transactions only
Weather-related facility closures only

stem: The six steps or components of the nursing process are often remembered using which acronym?
options: ADPIE
SOAPIE
PQRST
SBAR

stem: Nursing assessment is defined as which type of collection of data used to evaluate a client's health status?
options: A logical, systematic, and orderly collection of data
A random, unstructured collection of anecdotes with no method
A collection of data obtained exclusively from laboratory results with no interview
A collection of data obtained only after discharge

stem: Assessment provides the baseline data for formulating which subsequent step of the nursing process?
options: Nursing diagnosis and planning the care
Only the hospital billing department's invoice
Only the discharge paperwork, with no bearing on diagnosis
Only the visitor log at the nurses' station

stem: Which TWO types of assessment are specifically listed in the nursing process overview?
options: Initial (comprehensive) assessment and problem-focused assessment
Pre-admission assessment and post-mortem assessment only
Financial assessment and insurance eligibility assessment only
Weather assessment and transportation assessment only

stem: The PRIMARY source of data in nursing assessment is usually which of the following?
options: The patient, as the direct source
The hospital's billing department
The facility's maintenance staff
Unrelated media reports about the patient's neighborhood

stem: Secondary sources of data in nursing assessment include which of the following?
options: Family members and client records
Only the patient themselves
Only anonymous internet forums
Only the hospital cafeteria menu

stem: Objective data in nursing assessment, also referred to as signs or overt data, includes which examples?
options: Blood pressure and skin discoloration
The patient's reported feeling of worry
The patient's reported sensation of itching
The patient's subjective report of pain intensity alone

stem: Which of the following is explicitly listed as a source of information for nursing assessment, alongside health history and physical examination?
options: Diagnostic and laboratory investigation
The patient's personal social media activity
The hospital's parking lot occupancy rate
The nurse's personal daily schedule

stem: Most data obtained from history taking is subjective, and can be validated during which subsequent process?
options: Physical examination
Discharge planning exclusively
Billing reconciliation exclusively
Visitor registration exclusively

stem: Nursing history interview questions should progress in which direction?
options: From general to specific
From specific to general exclusively, with no flexibility
Randomly, with no logical progression at all
Only in a strict yes/no format with no open-ended questions

stem: The interview session used in history taking is divided into which three phases?
options: Introduction (joining), working, and termination phases
Billing, coding, and discharge phases
Preoperative, intraoperative, and postoperative phases
Morning, afternoon, and night shift phases

stem: During which phase of the nursing interview is the BULK of the patient information obtained?
options: The working phase
The introduction (joining) phase
The termination phase
A phase that does not exist in the standard three-phase structure

stem: During the termination phase of the nursing interview, what specifically occurs?
options: A summary of the discussion is presented so both patient and nurse can validate the perception of what occurred and what decisions were made
The nurse and patient meet for the very first time
All physical examination techniques are performed for the first time
The patient is discharged immediately with no further care planning

stem: Comprehensive physical examination is accomplished via which four techniques?
options: Inspection, palpation, percussion, and auscultation
Interviewing, billing, coding, and discharging
Charting, scheduling, filing, and archiving
Weighing, measuring height, checking ID, and signing consent

stem: Inspection, as a physical examination technique, involves which combination of senses?
options: Vision, hearing, and smell
Taste and touch exclusively
Only the sense of smell, with no visual component
Only the sense of hearing, with no visual component

stem: Percussion, as a physical examination technique, involves tapping the body to elicit sounds indicating which property of the underlying tissue?
options: Density
Temperature
Color
Taste

stem: Which percussion sound is described as a high-pitched, hollow sound typically heard over the stomach and bowel?
options: Tympany
Resonance
Dullness
Flatness

stem: Which percussion sound is described as a low-pitched sound typically heard over the lungs?
options: Resonance
Tympany
Flatness
Dullness

stem: Which percussion sound, of short duration, is typically heard over solid organs such as the liver?
options: Flat sound
Tympany
Resonance
Dull sound exclusively, never flat

stem: Auscultation, as a physical examination technique, is usually performed with the aid of which instrument?
options: A stethoscope
A percussion hammer
A reflex hammer exclusively, with no stethoscope
A tongue depressor exclusively

stem: Physical examination should be conducted systematically in which overall pattern?
options: From head to toe
Randomly, examining whichever body part is most convenient first
Only the chest and abdomen, omitting all other regions
Only the extremities, omitting the trunk and head

stem: Under the concept of primary health care, which simple diagnostic tests can be requested directly by the nurse?
options: Hb (hemoglobin), PCV (packed cell volume), blood grouping, and microscopic examination
Only full genomic sequencing
Only advanced cardiac catheterization studies
Only specialized nuclear medicine scans

stem: Gordon's Functional Health Pattern framework is specifically used to guide assessment that supports nurses in determining which type of diagnosis?
options: NANDA-I nursing diagnoses
Final medical diagnoses made exclusively by physicians
Insurance billing codes exclusively
Pharmacy inventory classifications exclusively

stem: Gordon's Functional Health Pattern assessment is usually performed at which point in a client's care?
options: When admitting a patient to a hospital or home care service
Only at the moment of discharge, never at admission
Only during a routine annual health fair unrelated to admission
Only after the patient has already been discharged for several months

stem: Nursing diagnosis is described as which numbered step of the nursing process?
options: The second step
The first step
The fifth step
The sixth and final step

stem: According to the ANA definition cited, nursing diagnosis is a clinical judgment about the client's response to which of the following?
options: Actual or potential health conditions or needs
The hospital's cafeteria menu choices
The weather forecast for the discharge date
The facility's visitor parking policy

stem: Which of the following is explicitly listed as a PURPOSE of nursing diagnosis?
options: Providing a common frame of reference and standardization of nursing language
Eliminating the need for any further assessment ever again
Replacing the physician's medical diagnosis entirely in every clinical scenario
Determining the hospital's annual operating budget

stem: The NANDA-I taxonomy organizes nursing diagnoses into how many domains and how many classes?
options: 13 domains and 47 classes
3 domains and 7 classes
100 domains and 500 classes
1 domain and 1 class

stem: Within the NANDA-I taxonomy, a 'domain' is best described as which of the following?
options: An area of interest, such as activity/rest, coping, or nutrition
A single, isolated patient symptom with no broader category
A billing code used exclusively for insurance purposes
A specific hospital ward location

stem: A problem-focused nursing diagnosis has which four components?
options: Label, definition, defining characteristics, and related factors
Billing code, insurance provider, co-pay amount, and deductible
Admission date, discharge date, room number, and bed number
Physician name, nurse name, ward name, and shift time

stem: In a nursing diagnosis, the 'label' or 'modifier' is best described as which part of speech, describing the human response?
options: An adjective, such as impaired, ineffective, deficient, or imbalanced
A proper noun naming a specific hospital
A numeral indicating bed number
A verb describing a surgical procedure

stem: In a nursing diagnosis, 'defining characteristics' are best described as which of the following?
options: Observable cues, such as signs, symptoms, or patient statements, that validate the existence of the problem
Unrelated demographic data such as the patient's occupation before illness
The exact dosage of medication prescribed
The specific brand name of medical equipment used

stem: In writing a problem-focused nursing diagnosis, the human response and the related factor are joined by which phrase?
options: 'Related to'
'In spite of'
'Regardless of'
'Unrelated to'

stem: In writing a problem-focused nursing diagnosis, the related factor and the defining characteristics are joined by which phrase?
options: 'As evidenced by'
'Related to'
'In contrast to'
'Despite the fact that'

stem: A risk nursing diagnosis has which three components, differing from the four components of a problem-focused diagnosis?
options: Label, definition, and risk factors
Label, defining characteristics, and related factors only, with no definition
Only a label, with no definition or risk factors at all
Admission date, discharge date, and room number

stem: A health promotion nursing diagnosis is a clinical judgment concerning which of the following?
options: Motivation and desire to increase well-being and actualize health potential
An already fully resolved health problem requiring no further action
A purely financial goal unrelated to health status
A diagnosis that can never apply to a healthy individual or group

stem: A syndrome nursing diagnosis is a clinical judgment concerning which of the following?
options: A specific cluster of nursing diagnoses that occur together and are best addressed through similar interventions
A single, isolated symptom with no relationship to any other diagnosis
A diagnosis that applies only to community-level assessments, never individuals
A diagnosis used exclusively in pediatric patients

stem: Chronic pain syndrome, as an example of a syndrome nursing diagnosis, includes chronic pain PLUS which additional diagnoses?
options: Disturbed sleep pattern, fatigue, impaired physical mobility, or social isolation
Only an unrelated diagnosis of acute appendicitis
Only a diagnosis of seasonal allergic rhinitis
Only a diagnosis of dental caries

stem: A nursing diagnosis typically contains which two parts?
options: A descriptor/modifier and the focus of the diagnosis
A billing code and an insurance authorization number
A room number and a bed number
A physician's signature and a notary stamp

stem: A problem-focused diagnosis should NOT automatically be viewed as more important than which other type of diagnosis, according to the material?
options: A risk diagnosis
A diagnosis made solely by a physician
A diagnosis unrelated to the patient's actual condition
A diagnosis based purely on billing considerations

stem: Formulating a nursing diagnosis consists of which four activities?
options: Collecting data, interpreting data, clustering information, and naming the cluster
Billing, coding, auditing, and archiving
Admitting, transferring, discharging, and readmitting
Scheduling, rescheduling, canceling, and rebooking

stem: Expected outcomes, identified during the outcome identification step, are best described as which type of goals?
options: Measurable, patient-focused goals derived from the patient's nursing diagnosis
Vague, immeasurable goals with no specific timeframe
Goals determined exclusively by hospital administration with no reference to diagnosis
Goals that are never reviewed or evaluated once written

stem: Short-term goals, as described in outcome identification, are best characterized by which feature?
options: They are of immediate concern and can be achieved quickly
They always take several years to achieve
They are never measurable in any way
They exclusively involve long-term rehabilitation

stem: Planning, as a phase of the nursing process, is described as a deliberative, systematic phase involving which two processes?
options: Decision making and problem solving
Billing and coding exclusively
Transportation scheduling and parking assignment exclusively
Visitor check-in and check-out exclusively

stem: Initial planning in the nursing process develops the initial comprehensive plan of care based on which assessment?
options: The admission assessment
A discharge assessment performed after the patient has already left
An assessment performed exclusively by a billing clerk
An assessment performed only by a hospital volunteer

stem: Ongoing planning in the nursing process occurs under which circumstance?
options: If the client's health status changes, requiring the nurse to set priorities for the shift
Only once, immediately before discharge, and never again before that point
Only when the hospital billing cycle changes
Only when the hospital changes its visiting hours policy

stem: A care plan may be standardized, OR it may be individualized to address which of the following?
options: Client needs that are not addressed by the standardized care plan
Only the hospital's billing requirements
Only the facility's parking allocation
Only the nurse's personal preferences, with no reference to the client at all

stem: Which THREE activities make up the planning process, according to the material?
options: Setting priorities, establishing goals/objectives, and selecting nursing interventions and activities
Billing, coding, and auditing
Admission, transfer, and discharge paperwork only
Ordering supplies, scheduling maintenance, and managing payroll

stem: Implementation, as a phase of the nursing process, is best described as which of the following?
options: The action phase in which the nurse carries out the plan of care
A phase that occurs only before assessment, never after planning
A purely theoretical phase with no direct patient contact
A phase limited exclusively to documentation with no direct care given

stem: If a nurse assigns some nursing actions to other staff members during implementation, what remains the assigning nurse's responsibility?
options: Ensuring that the care is given according to the nursing orders in the nursing process
Nothing further, since all responsibility transfers completely to the assigned staff member
Only completing unrelated billing paperwork
Only scheduling the next shift's staffing

stem: Which THREE nurse roles are specifically listed within the implementation phase of the nursing process?
options: Independent, dependent, and interdependent roles
Supervisory, administrative, and clerical roles only
Surgical, anesthetic, and radiological roles only
Financial, legal, and marketing roles only

stem: Which of the following is explicitly listed as an importance of documentation in the nursing process?
options: It provides evidence for evaluating purposes and ensures continuity of care
It eliminates the need for any further nursing assessment ever again
It replaces the need for direct patient communication entirely
It serves only as a record for the hospital's marketing department

stem: Evaluation, the final step of the nursing process, is defined as which of the following?
options: A planned, systematic comparison of the client's health status with the goals/expected outcomes
An unplanned, random comparison performed only once per year
A process performed exclusively by hospital administrators with no nurse involvement
A process that occurs only before the care plan is written

stem: Which of the following is explicitly listed among the evaluation indices of the nursing process?
options: Determining the client's progress toward achievement of the stated goals/expected outcomes
Calculating the hospital's total annual revenue
Assessing the facility's parking lot capacity
Reviewing the nurse's personal attendance record

stem: In evaluating progress toward goal achievement, which THREE possible conclusions may be reached?
options: The goal was met, partially met, or not met
The goal was billed, coded, or archived
The goal was admitted, transferred, or discharged
The goal was scheduled, rescheduled, or canceled

stem: The nursing process is described as a systematic process, meaning it proceeds in which manner?
options: Step by step
Entirely at random, with no fixed order
Only in reverse order, starting from evaluation
Only when convenient for hospital billing cycles

stem: CASE SCENARIO: A newly admitted client reports sunken eyes, dry lips, dry skin, and loss of skin turgor, following several days of vomiting and reduced oral intake. Which of the following is correctly written as a problem-focused nursing diagnosis for this client, using the proper format?
options: Deficient fluid volume related to active fluid loss as evidenced by sunken eyes, loss of skin turgor, dry lips, and dry skin
Deficient fluid volume as evidenced by active fluid loss related to sunken eyes and dry skin
Risk for deficient fluid volume related to sunken eyes and dry lips
Active fluid loss related to deficient fluid volume as evidenced by vomiting

stem: CASE SCENARIO: A client newly admitted to a skilled nursing facility has nursing diagnoses of decreased activity tolerance, impaired memory, readiness for enhanced health management, and risk for falls, with identified risk factors including poor vision, gait difficulty, and anxiety with relocation. Which diagnosis should the nurse prioritize FIRST, and why?
options: Risk for falls, because the identified risk factors combined with new admission and relocation create an immediate safety concern, even though it is a risk rather than a problem-focused diagnosis
Decreased activity tolerance, because problem-focused diagnoses are always ranked above risk diagnoses regardless of context
Readiness for enhanced health management, because health promotion diagnoses always take priority over safety concerns
Impaired memory, because cognitive diagnoses always outrank safety-related risk diagnoses

stem: CASE SCENARIO: During an admission interview, a nurse spends the first few minutes exchanging names, explaining her role, and helping the client feel comfortable before asking any health-related questions. Which phase of the nursing interview is this, and what is it intended to establish?
options: The introduction (joining) phase, intended to establish rapport and trust before the bulk of information is gathered in the working phase
The working phase, during which the bulk of clinical information is always obtained first
The termination phase, during which decisions made during the interview are summarized
A phase that does not exist in the standard three-phase structure of the nursing interview

stem: CASE SCENARIO: A nurse auscultates a client's lungs and hears a low-pitched sound consistent with normal lung tissue, then percusses over a area of suspected pneumonia and hears a dull sound. The nurse also palpates the abdomen to assess liver size and location. Which set of techniques and corresponding findings is correctly matched?
options: Auscultation revealed resonance consistent with normal lung tissue; percussion over the consolidated area revealed dullness consistent with pneumonia; palpation was used to assess the liver's size and location
Percussion revealed resonance; auscultation over the consolidated area revealed dullness; inspection was used to assess the liver's size and location
Palpation revealed tympany over the lungs; percussion assessed the liver by listening with a stethoscope; auscultation assessed organ size by touch
Inspection revealed a dull sound over the lungs; palpation revealed resonance over the liver; percussion was used to listen to heart sounds

stem: CASE SCENARIO: A client is being discharged home after a surgical admission. The nurse arranges for a home health aide to assist with wound care and schedules a follow-up home visit by a community health nurse. Which TYPE of planning does this represent, and at what point in the nurse-client relationship does this type of planning typically occur?
options: Discharge planning, which involves prescribing nursing intervention at home by caregivers or through a home visit, typically occurring as the nurse-client relationship in the acute setting is ending
Initial planning, which is based solely on the admission assessment and occurs only on the first day of hospitalization
Ongoing planning, which occurs only if the client's health status changes during a single shift
A type of planning that is not recognized within the nursing process and has no defined timing
